top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, independently reproduced achievement: the magic-wavelength idea (Katori) and its realization with strontium and the 1e-18 level of systematic control and comparison (Ye) have been built on by many laboratories worldwide. The work opens new tests of time, gravity and fundamental constants, and the Katori and Ye allocation with a citation tied to the lattice clock is precise and well bounded in scope. It is a clear step beyond earlier ion and microwave clocks, and I would rather award it than no one.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; she is an atomic theorist but no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye is documented, so only general field proximity
